item.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust Huang After Second Affair Report
item.description: The New York Times reported on Wednesday that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had an alleged extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of healthcare and one of his direct reports. Minutes later, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Huang. Nvidia shares fell more than 10 percent in after hours trading.

item.title: One Dead, 12 Hurt as Brooklyn Building Falls Into Construction Pit
item.description: A three story building in Flatbush, Brooklyn, collapsed into an open construction pit on Wednesday afternoon, killing one person and injuring 12 others, six of them critically, according to a Fire Department official. Firefighters dug through the rubble into the night as the search continued for people believed to be trapped beneath the wreckage.

item.title: Britain Backs Fractile With £500M in AI Chip Race
item.description: The British government has joined a funding round worth more than £500 million for Fractile, a startup building the chips that run artificial intelligence, in a bet that Britain can build its own AI hardware instead of buying it from abroad. The Series C values the London and Bristol company at more than £5 billion.

item.title: Irma P. Hall, Soul Food's Big Mama, Dies at 91
item.description: Irma P. Hall, the actress who played Big Mama Joe in Soul Food and won a Cannes prize for The Ladykillers, died on Tuesday in Dallas. She was 91. Her family announced her death on Wednesday, saying she died surrounded by her loved ones. No cause was given.

item.title: Yella Beezy Gets Life Without Parole for Mo3 Murder
item.description: A Dallas jury found rapper Yella Beezy guilty of capital murder on Wednesday for hiring the gunman who killed fellow rapper Mo3 in 2020. The judge sentenced him to life in prison without the possibility of parole, the mandatory punishment in Texas when prosecutors do not seek the death penalty.

item.title: Frankie Muniz Hospitalized After Daytona Practice Crash
item.description: Actor and NASCAR driver Frankie Muniz was taken to a hospital on Wednesday after crashing during practice at Daytona International Speedway. Ford Racing said the 40-year-old was "awake and alert" after the crash, which happened hours before the exhibition race he was due to drive in.

item.title: SS United States Sinks Off Florida to Become World's Largest Reef
item.description: The SS United States, the 990-foot ocean liner that still holds the transatlantic speed record it set in 1952, is going down off Florida today on purpose. Okaloosa County is sinking the ship, more than 100 feet longer than the Titanic, about 22 nautical miles southwest of Destin to become what the county calls the world's largest artificial reef.

item.title: Rex Ryan Arrested After Allegedly Running Over Two Pedestrians' Feet
item.description: Rex Ryan, the former NFL head coach and current ESPN analyst, was arrested in Nashville on Wednesday after police say he ran over the feet of two pedestrians with his pickup truck and drove away. Ryan, 63, turned himself in on six misdemeanor warrants and was released early Wednesday morning on a $6,000 bond.

item.title: Baby Found Alive in Buried Dog Crate After 24 Hours Underground
item.description: An 11-month-old boy was found alive in South Carolina on Tuesday after spending about 24 hours buried in a dog crate in the woods. Koah Sharpe was wrapped in a towel inside the crate, buried in a shallow hole, and deputies say the cold weather overnight probably slowed his breathing and gave them more time to find him.

item.title: Rox Raises $100M at $1.3B to Put AI Agents on Sales Teams
item.description: Rox, a two-year-old startup building an AI agent that does the work of enterprise sales teams, has raised $100 million at a $1.3 billion valuation. The Series B, announced Tuesday, was co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, and the company says its revenue grew more than tenfold in its first year in the market.

item.title: Virginia Madsen's Son Arrested in Fatal Alaska Hit-and-Run
item.description: Jack Sabato, the 32-year-old son of actors Virginia Madsen and Antonio Sabato Jr., has been arrested in Anchorage, Alaska, after a fatal hit-and-run that killed a pedestrian early Monday morning. Sabato faces two charges, was arraigned on Tuesday and remains in custody on a $5,000 bond, with a judge ordering him not to drive.

item.title: Madonna Takes the Dance Tent as Coachella Reveals 2027 Headliners
item.description: Coachella revealed its 2027 lineup, with Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA headlining the two weekends in Indio, California, and Madonna billed in the dance tent on Friday. The festival returns to the Empire Polo Club on April 9 to 11 and April 16 to 18, 2027, and passes go on sale Friday, November 13 at noon Pacific time.

item.title: Mark Robinson Files for Bankruptcy With $767 in the Bank
item.description: Mark Robinson, the former lieutenant governor of North Carolina, filed for Chapter 13 bankruptcy protection on November 3 with his wife Yolanda Hill, reporting $766.98 in liquid assets against nearly $800,000 in debt. The filing lands two years after his campaign for governor collapsed, and it puts the couple under court supervision as they seek to repay what they owe.

item.title: Reflect Orbital Raises $73.5 Million to Beam Sunlight After Dark
item.description: Reflect Orbital announced $73.5 million in new funding on November 10, taking its total funding past $100 million for satellites that reflect sunlight onto precise spots on Earth after dark. The money funds a first demonstration mission in the second quarter of 2027, which will test whether its mirrors can deploy and steer sunlight from orbit.

item.title: Vumedi Turns 100,000 Doctor Videos Into AI Answers
item.description: Vumedi expanded its AI powered physician learning on November 10, backed by a $104 million Series B growth investment from Oak HC/FT. The company's AI turns a library of more than 100,000 physician led videos and nearly 5,000 podcast episodes into answers for doctors, and physicians spend more than 4.3 million minutes a month learning on the platform.

item.title: Stacy Keach, TV's Mike Hammer, Dies at 85 After Heart Battle
item.description: Stacy Keach, the actor who played private detective Mike Hammer on television and built one of the most respected stage careers in America, has died at 85. He died Tuesday at his family home in Magdalenka, Poland, after what his wife called a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure.

item.title: Paul George Drops 36 on 76ers in Revenge Game Rout
item.description: Paul George scored 36 points against his old team as the Boston Celtics beat the Philadelphia 76ers 123-101 on Tuesday night, spoiling Jaylen Brown's revenge game and taking first place in the Eastern Conference. George, traded to Boston in the summer blockbuster that sent Brown to Philadelphia, torched the team that moved him in his first game back.

item.title: Georgia Takes No. 1 as Miami Falls and Ohio State Slides
item.description: Georgia is the new No. 1 team in the College Football Playoff rankings after the selection committee released its second Top 25 on Tuesday night. The Bulldogs climbed past Miami, which fell to seventh after its first loss of the season, while Ohio State slid all the way to No. 20 in a ranking full of movement.

item.title: Nidus Raises $30 Million to Put AI Robots in Defense Factories
item.description: Nidus, a New York robotics startup founded earlier this year, has raised $30 million to put AI-powered robots to work inside America's defense factories. The funding, backed by Kleiner Perkins and Costanoa, arrives just four months after the company started, and it already has more than $1 million in bookings from defense manufacturers.

item.title: Vikings Bring Back Kirk Cousins After Bills Expose Quarterback Crisis
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings acquired quarterback Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders on November 10 for a 2027 third round pick, bringing back the quarterback who led them for six seasons less than 24 hours after their offense collapsed in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

item.title: Jim Jordan Beats Scalise 106-73 to Lead House Republicans Into the Minority
item.description: House Republicans elected Rep. Jim Jordan of Ohio as their next leader on November 10, choosing the combative Judiciary Committee chairman over Majority Leader Steve Scalise in a 106-73 secret ballot vote one week after midterm losses cost the party control of Congress.

item.title: BBC Pulls Little Britain as Walliams Faces Sexual Misconduct Allegations
item.description: The BBC began removing programmes featuring David Walliams from iPlayer on November 10, including Little Britain, hours after a joint investigation by the Guardian and ITV News named the comedian in sexual misconduct allegations involving multiple women. Walliams denies all of the allegations against him.

item.title: House Blocks Hegseth Impeachment 211-204 as Massie Stands Alone
item.description: The House voted 211-204 on November 10 to send Rep. Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, blocking an immediate floor vote and handing Hegseth a reprieve with only weeks left in the current Congress.

item.title: Chiefs Trade Two Picks for Josh Downs to Give Mahomes a Weapon
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs acquired wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts on November 10, minutes before the NFL trade deadline, giving Patrick Mahomes a new target in exchange for two draft picks after weeks of searching for help at the position.

item.title: 49ers Trade Sixth Round Pick for Six Time Pro Bowler Keenan Allen
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers acquired wide receiver Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts on November 10 for a 2027 sixth round pick, adding a veteran pass catcher hours before the NFL trade deadline to a receiving room hit hard by injuries.

item.title: Path Robotics Raises $300 Million to Take Its Robots Beyond Welding
item.description: Path Robotics announced $300 million in Series E financing on November 10 at a post money valuation of $2.45 billion, a bet that the same artificial intelligence that taught its robots to weld can automate the rest of the factory floor.

item.title: Rockstar Confirms GTA 6 Is 30fps on Every Console, Even PS5 Pro
item.description: Rockstar Games confirmed on November 10 that Grand Theft Auto VI targets 30 frames per second on every console, ending months of speculation that the PlayStation 5 Pro would run the game at a higher frame rate with a performance mode of its own.

item.title: Ring Launches a $250 Drone Camera to Patrol Your Home
item.description: Ring launched Ring Robotics on November 10, a new line of autonomous security devices led by the $249.99 Ring Drone Cam, a flying indoor camera that patrols a home on its own, and the $999.99 Ring Rover Cam, a robot that patrols businesses. The drone ships January 27, 2027, and the rover ships December 16.

item.title: Mercor Raises $750 Million at $20 Billion Valuation to Train Enterprise AI
item.description: Mercor announced a $750 million Series D on November 10 that values the company at $20 billion, a round that included an employee tender and drew in Nvidia, Salesforce, and Zoom alongside the biggest venture firms in Silicon Valley. The money will accelerate Mercor's work helping enterprises measure, train, and improve AI agents on their own data and expertise.

item.title: Bob Boone, Catcher of Phillies' First World Series Title, Dies at 78
item.description: Bob Boone, the catcher who anchored the Philadelphia Phillies' first World Series championship team and stood at the center of baseball's first three generation family, has died at 78. His son Bret Boone announced the death on social media on Tuesday, and the Phillies said Boone died on Monday. No cause of death was announced.

item.title: Missed Vitamin K Shots Doubled as Newborn Bleeding Rose 347%
item.description: Two studies published November 5 found that fewer newborns are getting the vitamin K shot at birth, and that bleeding in infants is rising fast. One study of 5.2 million infants found the share missing the shot more than doubled since 2017, and a companion study found cases of vitamin K deficiency bleeding rose 347 percent over the same period.

item.title: FDA Orders Eye Warning on Ozempic, Zepbound and Every GLP-1 Drug
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration on November 9 ordered every maker of GLP-1 diabetes and weight loss drugs to add a warning about a rare eye condition that can cause sudden, permanent vision loss in one eye. The warning covers Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound, and every other drug in the class.

item.title: Primordial Labs Raises $18M to Let Soldiers Command Machines by Voice
item.description: Primordial Labs announced on November 10 that it has raised $18 million in Series A funding to scale Anura, its natural language command and control platform for military systems. Ballistic Ventures led the round, with Squadra Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures taking part, and the company says it is already delivering licenses to the Army and special operations units.

item.title: US Citizen Shot by ICE Sues for $25M After Charges Are Dropped
item.description: Carlos Jimenez, a US citizen from Ontario, California, filed a 54-page federal lawsuit on November 6 seeking more than $25 million from the Trump administration and several federal officers. The lawsuit alleges that an ICE officer shot him in the back and shoulder during an immigration operation in October 2025 and that prosecutors then pursued him on fabricated evidence, and the criminal charges against him were dismissed with prejudice on November 2.

item.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Pre-Loading Opens Today Ahead of November 19 Launch
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI pre-loading opens today, November 10, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, nine days before the game launches on November 19. Rockstar Games set the download at up to 212 GB, so players need to clear space now if they want to play the moment the game unlocks.

item.title: Bills Beat Vikings 23-6 as Carson Wentz Gets Benched in Prime Time
item.description: The Buffalo Bills beat the Minnesota Vikings 23-6 on Monday Night Football, and the Vikings benched quarterback Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter after one of the worst starts of his career. Wentz completed 8 of 25 passes for 81 yards with two interceptions before second year pro Max Brosmer finished the game.

item.title: Coframe Raises $25 Million to Build Websites That Improve Themselves
item.description: Coframe has raised $35 million in total funding, including a $25 million Series A co-led by Khosla Ventures and Hanabi Capital, to build websites, landing pages and ads that continuously generate, test and improve themselves instead of waiting for the next redesign.

item.title: geniosAI Emerges From Stealth With $19.1 Million to Make AI Finance Traceable
item.description: geniosAI has emerged from stealth with $19.1 million in combined seed and Series A funding from FactSet, Zoom and General Catalyst, with the Series A led by FactSet, to build AI that shows financial institutions exactly how it reached every answer.

item.title: Russell Brand Sentenced to 10 Years and Six Months in Prison for Rape and Sexual Assault
item.description: A judge at Southwark Crown Court sentenced Russell Brand to 10 years and six months in prison on November 9, four days after a jury convicted the comedian and actor of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others in offences dating back to 2004.

item.title: Thomas Massie Files Eight Articles of Impeachment Against Pete Hegseth and Forces a House Vote
item.description: Rep. Thomas Massie refiled eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the House floor on November 9, forcing the House to act on removing one of President Donald Trump's most prominent cabinet secretaries within two legislative days.

item.title: Eagles Trade Jordan Davis to the Jaguars for a 2027 First Round Pick and a 2029 Second Rounder
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars on November 9 for a 2027 first round pick and a 2029 second round pick, a blockbuster deal struck less than 24 hours before the NFL trade deadline.

item.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 With Faster Output and Lower Prices
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on November 9, its most capable AI models yet, promising faster responses, stronger coding and science results, and lower prices just over two months after the 5.1 versions arrived and ahead of a planned IPO.

item.title: Project Omega Raises $80 Million to Recycle Nuclear Fuel and Build Long Duration Power Systems
item.description: Project Omega raised $80 million in Series A financing on November 9 to build nuclear refineries that turn America's used nuclear fuel into reactor fuel, strategic isotopes and power systems that run for years without refueling, in a bet on a domestic nuclear fuel cycle.

item.title: Spines Raises $64 Million as AI Publishing Platform Hits a $50 Million Revenue Run Rate
item.description: Spines secured $64 million in growth capital on November 9, combining a $29 million Series A-1 equity round with a $35 million non-dilutive growth facility, as the AI publishing platform reported a $50 million revenue run rate and 400 percent year over year growth.

item.title: James Gunn and Peter Safran Step Down at DC Studios as Marvel Veteran Jeremy Latcham Takes Over
item.description: James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as the heads of DC Studios after four years, and former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham will take over as president and chief creative officer on December 1. Skydance, which now owns the studio through its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, announced the leadership change on Monday.

item.title: Jaguars Land Pro Bowl Safety Jessie Bates in Trade Deadline Deal With Falcons
item.description: The Jacksonville Jaguars acquired Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons on Monday, sending two future draft picks to Atlanta a day before the NFL trade deadline. The move loads up a defense that already leads the AFC South for a playoff push, and it leaves the Falcons selling after a 3-6 start.

item.title: Nominal Raises $240 Million at a $3 Billion Valuation to Build the Intelligence Platform for Hardware Engineering
item.description: Nominal announced on November 9 that it has raised a $240 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation, led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and co-led by Insight Partners. The hardware intelligence platform serves more than 80 commercial and government organizations, including five of the seven largest defense contractors.

item.title: Onodrim Raises $300 Million at a $1.3 Billion Valuation to Buy and Modernize European Defense Suppliers
item.description: Onodrim Industries announced on November 9 that it has raised a $300 million Series A led by Lux Capital, valuing the Amsterdam company at $1.3 billion. The European defense and industrial platform will use the money to buy established manufacturers and modernize them with technology.

item.title: Rochelle Fleming, Lead Singer of Disco Group First Choice, Dies at 72
item.description: Rochelle Fleming, the founding lead singer of the Philadelphia soul and disco group First Choice, died on November 5 in Philadelphia at 72. Her manager announced the death on Saturday in a post on her official Instagram page, and no cause of death was disclosed.

item.title: Trump Tells 60 Minutes He Cannot Forgive His Enemies, Even to Reach Heaven
item.description: President Donald Trump said in a 60 Minutes interview that he cannot forgive his political enemies, even if forgiveness were the price of reaching heaven, and admitted his deportation policy went too tough. The interview, recorded Friday at the White House and aired Sunday, was his first sit-down since Republicans lost both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections.

item.title: Mike Tirico Misses Sunday Night Football Over Health Issue as Noah Eagle Fills In
item.description: NBC play-by-play voice Mike Tirico missed Sunday Night Football on November 8 because of a health issue, hours before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers played the Chicago Bears in Chicago. Noah Eagle stepped in at short notice to call the game, and Tirico said he expects to be back in the booth for next Sunday's game in Cincinnati.

item.title: Nvidia CEO honey-trapped by alleged Chinese spy
item.description: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on Sunday into reports that founder and CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, hours after Huang told employees he had been unfaithful to his wife. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

item.title: Delhi Air Crosses Into Severe Range the Morning After Diwali as Emergency Curbs Stay in Force
item.description: Delhi woke on Monday to thick smog and air quality in the severe range at monitoring stations across the capital, a day after Diwali firecrackers added to already foul air. The city's overall reading stayed in the "very poor" band while emergency restrictions imposed last week remained in force.

item.title: Microsoft Workers Call Work "Joyless" in Open Letter Protesting the Company's AI Push
item.description: Microsoft workers have gone public with an open letter that calls working at the company "joyless and demoralizing" and accuses its leadership of chasing artificial intelligence at any cost. The letter surfaced days after Microsoft offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees, and it turns a workforce story into a public fight over how AI is changing work.

item.title: New Zealand Election Ends With No Winner as Labour Edges National by 3,650 Votes
item.description: New Zealanders voted on Saturday and still do not know who will govern them. The preliminary count puts Labour ahead of National by just 3,650 votes, yet National holds more seats, and neither side can form a government until nearly 400,000 special votes are counted and the official result lands on November 27.

item.title: One Cyclist Killed and More Than a Dozen Hurt as Suspected Impaired Driver Plows Into North Carolina Group Ride
item.description: A 63 year old cyclist was killed and more than a dozen riders were hurt on Saturday morning when a suspected impaired driver crossed the center line and plowed into a Capital Cycling Club group ride in Wake County, North Carolina. The North Carolina State Highway Patrol arrested the 76 year old driver at the scene and charged him with felony death by vehicle and multiple counts tied to the injuries and to leaving the scene.

item.title: Axon Puts $1.2 Billion Into Skydio and Becomes Its Exclusive Public Safety Distributor
item.description: Axon is investing an additional $1.2 billion in Skydio, lifting its fully diluted ownership in the drone maker to 37 percent and becoming the exclusive distributor of Skydio drones to public safety agencies in the United States and Canada. Axon announced the investment on November 5, 2026, in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, calling it the largest single investment in the company's history.

item.title: Fishermen Pull Royal Caribbean Pianist From the Pacific After Nine Hours in the Water
item.description: Two fishermen from Newport Beach pulled a Royal Caribbean crew member from the Pacific Ocean about 20 miles off the California coast on Friday after he spent roughly nine hours treading water, and the man told them he was a pianist on the cruise ship Ovation of the Seas. The man was taken to a hospital and is expected to survive, and the United States Coast Guard is investigating how he went overboard.

item.title: FDA Adds 21st Cinnamon Product to Lead Alert as Wise Wife Recall Reaches 14 States
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration has added a 21st ground cinnamon product to its public health alert on lead contamination, after a Connecticut laboratory found elevated lead in Wise Wife brand cinnamon and the distributor recalled the product in 14 states. SLR Food Distribution announced the recall on October 29, 2026, and the FDA posted the company's announcement the same day.

item.title: Trump Orders Justice Department to Investigate Democrats Over Alleged Threats to Donors
item.description: President Donald Trump has ordered the Department of Justice to investigate Democratic lawmakers, accusing them of threatening administration officials and Republican donors with impeachment and imprisonment. Trump issued the order in two posts on Truth Social late on Saturday, calling the alleged threats extortion at the highest level and saying those responsible should go to jail.

item.title: Gunman Kills Six in Krakow Main Square as Three More Bodies Are Found at His Home
item.description: A gunman drove into Krakow's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon and opened fire on crowds, killing six people and wounding 15 before police shot and arrested him, and hours later three more bodies were found at his home as Poland's prime minister called the attack terrorism.

item.title: Berkshire Hathaway Buys Back $9.6 Billion of Stock as Operating Profit Falls
item.description: Berkshire Hathaway bought back $9.6 billion of its own stock in the third quarter, its biggest quarterly repurchase of the year, even as operating earnings fell 5.8 percent. The results, released on Saturday, show the conglomerate leaning harder on buybacks in Greg Abel's first year as chief executive.

item.title: Google Takes Over Crusoe's Wyoming Campus as $17 Billion Data Center Build Begins
item.description: Google has acquired the Wyoming data center site that startup Crusoe spent more than a year preparing, taking direct control of the campus one day after announcing a $17 billion investment in its first data center in the state. Crusoe confirmed the sale on November 6, saying its pre-development work on the southeast Wyoming project is complete.

item.title: Michael Sanft, Lawyer Who Defended Keefe D in Tupac Murder Trial, Dies
item.description: Michael Sanft, the Las Vegas lawyer who defended Duane "Keefe D" Davis in the murder trial over Tupac Shakur's death, has died. The Clark County coroner's office confirmed his death on Friday, November 6, and his cause of death is pending.

item.title: US Added 165,000 Jobs in October as Unemployment Eased to 4.1%
item.description: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday, while the unemployment rate eased to 4.1 percent. The gain ran well above the recent monthly pace, and revisions added 84,000 jobs to August and September, giving the labor market a stronger footing heading into the final weeks of the year.

item.title: Physicl Raises $10 Million to Train Robots on the Edge Cases They Get Wrong
item.description: Physicl, a Paris startup building synthetic training data for physical AI, has raised $10 million in seed funding led by Inovia Capital. The company also launched Studio, a tool that generates the rare situations robots and world models get wrong.

item.title: Navy Removes Blue Angels Pilot Scott Laux Before Season Finale in Pensacola
item.description: The U.S. Navy has removed Marine Corps Maj. Scott Laux, the Blue Angels' No. 6 opposing solo pilot, from the flight demonstration squadron, and the team flew with five jets instead of six at its homecoming air show in Pensacola on Friday. The Navy confirmed the removal on November 6 but has not said what Laux did to prompt it.

item.title: Sony Brings Back Its 1979 Walkman Headphones as the $60 MDR-3R
item.description: Sony has revived the headphones that shipped with the first Walkman, announcing the MDR-3R on November 5 at $59.99. The wired USB-C model copies the 1979 original down to its 23mm drivers and orange ear pads, and a Stranger Things edition follows at $79.99.

item.title: Trump Names Stephen Miller White House Chief of Staff, Replacing Susie Wiles
item.description: President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller, his deputy chief of staff for policy, as the next White House chief of staff. Miller takes over from Susie Wiles on Monday, November 9, in a shakeup that follows heavy Republican losses in the midterm elections.

item.title: Synctera Raises $24.5 Million as Banks Return to Banking as a Service
item.description: Synctera has raised $24.5 million in new funding, the embedded finance company announced November 6, bringing its total funding to $126.7 million. The round lands as banks return to banking as a service, with Main Street Bank joining as its newest sponsor bank.

item.title: FBI Arrests Thomas Markle, Meghan's Father, on Child Sexual Abuse Material Charge
item.description: The FBI has arrested Thomas Wayne Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, on a federal charge of possessing child sexual abuse material. Agents took the 82-year-old into custody at his senior living home in Lakeland, Florida, on Friday.

item.title: Trump Offers UFC Chief Dana White the White House Press Secretary Job
item.description: President Donald Trump has offered the White House press secretary job to Dana White, the president and chief executive of the UFC, in a post on Truth Social on Saturday. Trump asked White to bring six mixed martial arts fighters with him as assistants, and it remains unclear whether the offer was serious or a joke.

item.title: Artemis II Tore Holes in the Upper Atmosphere Big Enough to Shift GPS Readings
item.description: NASA's Artemis II mission punched temporary holes in Earth's upper atmosphere so large they stretched 3,100 miles across North America, according to a study reported on November 4. The disturbances were strong enough to shift GPS readings by several metres, a warning for self driving cars and drones as heavy launches become routine.

item.title: Florida Flood Emergency Grows to 14 Counties as Rivers Keep Rising
item.description: Record rainfall across central Florida has killed two people in Palm Bay, forced hundreds of rescues and pushed the state of emergency to 14 counties, with rivers still rising days after the rain stopped. More than 24 inches fell near Malabar in about two days, a deluge the National Weather Service called a once in a thousand year event.

item.title: IRS Raises 2027 Tax Brackets and Standard Deduction
item.description: The Internal Revenue Service has released the 2027 tax brackets and standard deduction, lifting the income thresholds at every rate and raising the standard deduction to $16,600 for single filers and $33,200 for married couples filing jointly. The new figures apply to income earned in 2027 and the tax returns filed in early 2028.

item.title: Jay Rockefeller, Five-Term Senator and Children's Health Champion, Dies at 89
item.description: Former West Virginia governor and five-term United States Senator Jay Rockefeller has died at 89. Rockefeller died at his home in Washington, and his death was announced on Friday, November 6. He spent five decades in West Virginia public life, and he wrote the children's health insurance program that still covers millions of American kids.

item.title: Kalepa Raises $75 Million to Put AI Across Insurance Underwriting
item.description: Kalepa has raised $75 million in Series B funding at a $470 million valuation to expand its artificial intelligence software for insurers. The company announced the round on November 5, led by Updata Partners, five years after its last funding round. Kalepa has tripled its revenue and customer count in the past year while staying cash flow positive.

item.title: Nasdaq Plunges 5.5 Percent in Worst Day in 19 Months as AI Selloff Deepens
item.description: US stocks tumbled on Thursday, November 5, as the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52 percent in its worst day in 19 months. A ferocious selloff in chip and data center stocks erased the entire post election rally in a single session and pushed the Nasdaq into correction territory.

item.title: Nooks Lands $500 Million to Build AI Sales Agents and Launches Node
item.description: Nooks has secured $500 million in growth capital from General Catalyst and launched Node, an AI personal assistant for sales, alongside a new Revenue Agent Platform that covers the full sales cycle. The company announced the package on November 4, pairing the funding with a product launch aimed at putting AI agents on every sales team.

item.title: Paraguay President Resigns After Ueno Bank Collapse, Then Is Impeached Minutes Later
item.description: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigned on Thursday, November 5, days after the collapse of Ueno Bank froze the savings of about 3 million people. Minutes after he announced his resignation, the lower house of Congress voted 78 to 0 to impeach him, ending his presidency in the country's biggest political crisis in years.

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Retires From International Football After 23 Years With Portugal
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football, closing a 23 year career with Portugal that produced a record 146 goals in 234 appearances. The 41 year old announced the decision on Thursday, November 5, 2026, in a video posted to his social media accounts, telling supporters the time had come to hand back the No. 7 shirt.

item.title: Sentra Raises $150 Million to Police What AI Agents Can Reach in Corporate Data
item.description: Sentra, a data security startup built for the age of AI agents, has raised $150 million in a Series C round led by Capital One Ventures. The company says the money will expand software that maps and limits the sensitive corporate data that employees, apps and AI agents can touch.

item.title: Shield AI Buys Radar Maker Echodyne for $5.3 Billion and Raises $2.5 Billion at a $28.8 Billion Valuation
item.description: Shield AI has agreed to acquire radar maker Echodyne in a transaction valued at $5.3 billion and is raising $2.5 billion to fund the deal, a package that values the defense technology company at $28.8 billion. Shield announced both moves on November 5, 2026, pairing its largest acquisition with its largest financing in a single day.

item.title: Tesla Winds Down Cybertruck Production to Make Room for Cybercabs
item.description: Tesla will wind down production of the Cybertruck around the middle of 2027, chief executive Elon Musk said on Friday, November 6. The electric pickup will give up its line at Gigafactory Texas so the plant can build more Cybercabs, Tesla's robotaxi. The move ends a troubled run for a truck that never came close to its sales targets.

item.title: Wonder Files Confidentially for an IPO After Building a Food Empire on Delivery and Restaurants
item.description: Wonder Group has confidentially filed for an initial public offering, taking the first formal step toward the public markets after years of aggressive expansion. The food technology company announced on November 5, 2026 that it has submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 to the Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed offering of its Class A common stock.

item.title: Agility Robotics Starts Trading on Nasdaq as the First Pure-Play Humanoid Robot Stock
item.description: Agility Robotics said on November 4 that it had completed its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI, and its shares begin trading on the Nasdaq today, November 5, under the ticker AGLT. The listing makes Agility the first US-listed company devoted entirely to humanoid robots with machines already working for paying customers.

item.title: Bob Dylan Met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican and Traded His Autobiography for a Rosary
item.description: Pope Leo XIV received Bob Dylan in a private audience at the Vatican on Wednesday, November 4, bringing together the 85-year-old Nobel laureate and the pope who quoted his lyrics in a book on disarmament earlier this year. The meeting ended with an exchange of gifts: a rosary from the pope and a copy of Dylan's autobiography from the singer.

item.title: Bob Heinz, Two Time Super Bowl Champion From the Dolphins' Undefeated 1972 Team, Dies at 79
item.description: Bob Heinz, the defensive tackle who started on the Miami Dolphins teams that won back to back Super Bowls and completed the NFL's only undefeated season in 1972, died on October 31, 2026, at his home in Fresno, California. He was 79.

item.title: EloElo Group Raises $80 Million to Take Its Microdrama Platform Beyond India
item.description: EloElo Group, the Bengaluru company behind Story TV, has raised $80 million in a Series C round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal, the company announced on November 4, 2026. The round takes EloElo's total capital raised to $130 million and will fund more original content, an international launch, and further investment in its AI creative suite.

item.title: Harbinger Raises $240 Million to Take Its Electric Truck Technology Into Defense and Energy Storage
item.description: Harbinger, the electric truck maker building an industrial technology platform, has raised $240 million in a Series D funding round as it expands beyond commercial vehicles into defense, energy storage, power generation, and autonomy software. The company announced the round on November 5, 2026, and said it has now raised more than $650 million since its founding in 2021.

item.title: Outback Steakhouse Franchisee Files for Bankruptcy After Closing 10 Restaurants, and the Chain's Parent Moves to Buy the Rest
item.description: Out West Restaurant Group, the franchisee that runs 61 Outback Steakhouse restaurants across the western United States, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Delaware on November 2, 2026, after closing 10 restaurants in October. Bloomin' Brands, the chain's parent company, moved the same week to buy the remaining restaurants for $26.3 million.

item.title: PlayStation Store Black Friday Deals Open November 4 With Up to 75% Off Thousands of Games
item.description: Sony's PlayStation Store Black Friday Deals open Wednesday, November 4, with discounts of up to 75% across thousands of PS5, PS4, and PS VR2 games, expansions, and downloadable content, Sony announced on PlayStation.Blog on November 3, 2026. The sale runs through Monday, November 30, refreshes with new titles on November 16, and ends some discounts early on November 20.

item.title: Pliant Raises $80 Million to Open Its B2B Payments Platform to AI Agents
item.description: Pliant, a Berlin fintech that builds payment infrastructure for businesses, has raised $80 million in a Series C round led by Seaya Nova and Speedinvest, the company announced on November 4, 2026. The round follows three straight years in which Pliant doubled its business, and it comes shortly after the company passed $100 million in annual recurring revenue.

item.title: A Single New Jersey Ticket Won the $847 Million Powerball Jackpot
item.description: A single ticket sold in New Jersey won the $847 million Powerball jackpot in the drawing on Wednesday, November 4, matching all six numbers to take the ninth-largest prize in the game's history. The winner can take the full $847 million as an annuity or a $363.1 million lump sum, and both figures are before taxes.

item.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault After Trial in London
item.description: A jury at Southwark Crown Court in London convicted comedian Russell Brand on November 5, 2026, of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The verdicts ended a four week trial over offences against four women between 2004 and 2009, and the judge remanded Brand in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, November 9.

item.title: Titan OS Raises $46 Million to Take Its Smart TV System Beyond Europe
item.description: Titan OS, the Barcelona company whose software powers the home screens of Philips, Sharp, JVC, and other television brands, has raised $46 million in new financing, the company announced on November 4, 2026. The round combines fresh equity from existing investors with a credit facility from funds managed by BlackRock, and it lifts Titan OS's total funding to $110 million.

item.title: Traversal Raises $120 Million at a $1 Billion Valuation to Build the AI Site Reliability Engineer
item.description: Traversal, a New York startup building AI agents that diagnose, fix, and prevent software outages, has raised $120 million in a Series B round at a $1 billion valuation, the company announced on November 3, 2026. Kleiner Perkins, Redpoint Ventures, and Khosla Ventures co-led the round, which lifts Traversal's total funding to $173 million.

item.title: Zipline Raises $1.5 Billion at a $21.5 Billion Valuation as Walmart Signs for 300 More Drone Sites
item.description: Zipline, the drone delivery company, has raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion post-money valuation and signed a new national agreement with Walmart to launch 300 additional drone delivery sites across the United States. The company announced both deals on November 5, 2026, and said the money will fund expanded American manufacturing, more hiring, and a nationwide delivery network.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed Wins Michigan Senate Race, Becoming the First Muslim Elected to the US Senate
item.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan's United States Senate race on November 3, winning an open seat and becoming the first Muslim ever elected to the Senate. The Associated Press called the race for El-Sayed in the early hours of Wednesday, November 4, capping a hard-fought campaign in one of the country's most closely watched Senate contests.

item.title: Larridin Raises $30 Million to Show Companies What Their AI Spending Actually Produces
item.description: Larridin, a South San Francisco startup that measures the business value of enterprise AI, has raised $30 million in Series A funding led by Pelion Ventures. The round brings the company's total funding to $47 million as businesses demand proof that their AI budgets are producing real work.

item.title: Microsoft Priced a $25 Billion Bond Sale. Closing Is Expected Today.
item.description: Microsoft priced a $25 billion offering of senior unsecured notes on October 29, and the offering is expected to close on November 4, 2026. The sale spans ten tranches with maturities from 2028 to 2066, and Microsoft says the proceeds will fund general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures.

item.title: Rachel Apa, 24, Dies After Collapsing Near the Finish of Her First New York City Marathon
item.description: Rachel Apa, a 24 year old runner from Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, died on Sunday, November 1, after collapsing near mile 24 of the New York City Marathon, about two miles from the finish line in Central Park. She was running her first marathon, in memory of her grandfather, when she collapsed at about 1:30 p.m. local time.

item.title: Salesforce Signs Deal to Acquire Voice AI Company Cresta
item.description: Salesforce has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, the voice-first operating system for customer experience, bringing AI voice agents for complex customer calls into Service Cloud. Salesforce announced the agreement on November 2, 2026, and expects it to close in the first quarter of fiscal year 2028, subject to regulatory approvals. No purchase price is disclosed in the announcement.

item.title: Apple Reports a Record $114.5 Billion September Quarter on Strong iPhone Sales
item.description: Apple reported November 2 that revenue reached $114.5 billion in its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, up 12 percent from a year earlier and a record for a September quarter. Diluted earnings per share rose 14 percent to $2.10, also a September quarter record, in the first earnings report since John Ternus became chief executive.

item.title: Marvell to Buy Lumentum in a $115 Billion All-Stock Bet on Optical AI Connections
item.description: Marvell Technology has agreed to acquire optical components maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal worth an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, the two companies announced November 2. The combination joins Marvell's chip and electrical interconnect business with Lumentum's lasers and optical parts, betting that the wiring inside AI data centers is shifting from copper to light.

item.title: Check the Bottle: 3,744 Bottles of a Generic Blood Pressure Pill Were Recalled
item.description: Searches for olmesartan surged in the United States this week as word spread about a nationwide recall of a generic three in one blood pressure pill. Macleods Pharma USA recalled 3,744 bottles in two lots after the tablets failed a dissolution test, and the Food and Drug Administration classified the recall as Class II on October 26, 2026.

item.title: Tutor Intelligence Raises $75 Million to Put Robot Workers on Factory and Warehouse Floors
item.description: Tutor Intelligence announced November 2 that it has raised a $75 million Series B round led by Andreessen Horowitz, bringing the Watertown, Massachusetts robotics company's total capital raised to $117 million. The funding will train Tutor's frontier robot foundation models and build and deploy Sonny and Cassie, its robot workers.

item.title: Flash Flooding Forces Sedona Evacuations as Oak Creek Surges Past Flood Stage
item.description: Flash flooding on Oak Creek forced immediate evacuations in Sedona, Arizona, on Sunday, November 1, closed highways across northern Arizona, and left a flood warning in place into Monday morning as water levels fell in Sedona but stayed above flood stage downstream at Cornville.

item.title: Florida State Fires Mike Norvell After Clemson Loss, Taking On a Buyout Near $50 Million
item.description: Florida State fired head football coach Mike Norvell on Sunday, November 1, one day after a 36-24 home loss to Clemson dropped the Seminoles to 3-5 on the season. The decision ends Norvell's tenure after more than six seasons in Tallahassee, with former Seminole quarterback Rick Stockstill named interim head coach and a national search for a successor already underway.

item.title: Jack Campbell Hospitalized Overnight After Neck Injury in Lions Win Over Vikings
item.description: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was taken to a local hospital on Sunday, November 1, after suffering a neck injury during the Lions 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings, and the team said he would remain in the hospital overnight for continued evaluation and monitoring.

item.title: Karl Bushby Walks Home After 28 Years and About 31,000 Miles
item.description: Karl Bushby walked up to his mother's front door in Hull, England, on Monday, November 2, 2026, and finished a walk he started in Chile 28 years earlier. The 57-year-old former paratrooper covered about 31,000 miles across 30 countries without using motorized transport to move forward, and crowds welcomed him home.

item.title: Nine Killed as Learjet 60 Crashes in a Palm Beach County Neighborhood
item.description: All nine people aboard a Learjet 60 were killed on Sunday, November 1, when the business jet crashed in a residential area of Palm Beach County, Florida, after departing Austin, Texas, for the Bahamas. United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the deaths, and the National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation into what caused the crash.

item.title: Northwood Space Raises $375 Million to Build the Ground Network for Satellites
item.description: Northwood Space has closed a $375 million Series C round to scale the shared ground network that connects satellites to Earth, the Torrance, California company announced November 2. The funding will speed delivery on existing contracts, expand hiring, and build out a global network for commercial, United States government, and allied space missions.

item.title: Nintendo Reveals the Team Behind the Ocarina of Time Remake and One Change It Reversed
item.description: Nintendo has named the team remaking The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and revealed a modern convenience the developers tried and then removed, in the first two parts of its Ask the Developer interview published November 2. The full remake launches Thursday, November 5, as a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive.

item.title: Canelo Alvarez Reclaimed the WBC Title by Beating Christian Mbilli in Riyadh
item.description: Canelo Alvarez beat Christian Mbilli by unanimous decision over 12 rounds on October 31 in Riyadh, reclaiming the WBC super middleweight title more than a year after losing his undisputed championship to Terence Crawford. The win handed Mbilli his first professional defeat and made Alvarez a world champion again at 36.

item.title: Senator Chris Murphy Hospitalized After a Stroke, His Office Says He Is Awake and Alert
item.description: Connecticut Democratic Senator Chris Murphy was hospitalized after suffering a stroke on Saturday afternoon, his office said on Sunday, November 1, and he is now monitored at Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore. His chief of staff said doctors are encouraged, he is awake and alert and responding well, and the office is optimistic he will make a full recovery.

item.title: Clocks Fall Back on November 1 as Daylight Saving Time Ends for 2026
item.description: Most of the United States returns to standard time at 2 a.m. on Sunday, November 1, 2026, when clocks move back one hour to 1 a.m. and the hour between 1 and 2 a.m. happens twice. The change brings an extra hour of sleep and earlier sunsets, and it arrives even though the House voted to end the clock changes.

item.title: Democrat Haley Stevens Endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate Race Two Days Before the Vote
item.description: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the United States Senate on Sunday, November 1, breaking with her party's nominee two days before voters decide a race that could help determine Senate control. Stevens announced it in a video after appearing with Rogers at a Detroit church service, turning a feud into a split in the final hours.

item.title: Inés Gómez Mont, Identified in Reports, Was Secured in Miami After Five Years as a Fugitive
item.description: Mexico's attorney general's office confirmed on October 30, 2026 that a woman it identified only as "Inés N" was secured in Miami, Florida, after information was shared with the United States government. Reports identified her as former television host Inés Gómez Mont, out of Mexican authorities' reach since warrants were issued in 2021.

item.title: Gabby Williams Scored 28 in the Second Half as the Valkyries Won Their First WNBA Title
item.description: Gabby Williams scored 30 points and the Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 on October 31, winning the franchise's first WNBA championship in only its second season. Williams scored 28 of her points after halftime and was named Finals MVP.

item.title: Dataline Raises $10.6 Million to Build a Data Network for AI Agents
item.description: Dataline, a decentralized network that sells data to AI agents, has raised $10.6 million in a round co-led by Lattice and Samsung-backed Dispersion Capital, the company announced October 31. The raise arrives with a partner cohort spanning prediction markets Polymarket and Kalshi and blockchains Base and Robinhood Chain.

item.title: Intel's Data Center Sales Surged 78 Percent, but a Weak Forecast Hit the Stock
item.description: Intel reported third quarter revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21 percent from a year earlier, as sales of its data center chips surged 78 percent on demand for AI servers. But the chipmaker forecast a weaker fourth quarter than Wall Street expected, and its shares fell sharply in after-hours trading.

item.title: A Judge Let the McRib Lawsuit Proceed. The Question Is Whether a Rib Shaped Patty Promises Rib Meat
item.description: A federal judge in Chicago ruled on October 30 that McDonald's must face a proposed class action claiming the McRib misleads customers about its meat. The judge rejected the company's bid to throw the case out, keeping alive claims that the sandwich's name and rib shaped patty promise pork rib meat that buyers do not get.

item.title: Nasdaq Drops 2.86 Percent in Worst Day Since June as AI Spending Fears Roil Tech
item.description: US stocks tumbled on Friday, October 30, as the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.86 percent in its worst day since June. Disappointing results from Intel and Amazon deepened worries that massive spending on artificial intelligence is not paying off fast enough, capping a brutal October for technology shares.

item.title: Police Surround Poland's Constitutional Tribunal After Its President Is Suspended
item.description: Police surrounded Poland's Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw on Friday night after a rival judge suspended the court's president and deputy, plunging the country into a constitutional standoff. President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane back from a trip to Senegal as protesters gathered outside the court and the tribunal's leadership accused the government of staging a coup.

item.title: Reddit's Revenue Jumped 53 Percent, but Shrinking US Users Spooked Investors
item.description: Reddit reported third quarter revenue of $895 million, up 53 percent from a year earlier, with profit of $283 million and advertising up 54 percent. But daily users in the United States fell 2 percent, search referrals kept sliding, and fourth quarter guidance came in below Wall Street's hopes, sending shares sharply lower.

item.title: Coroner Links Mad Max Actor Richard Norton's Death to Unapproved Peptides
item.description: A Victorian coroner has found that Australian actor and martial artist Richard Norton's death was triggered by an injection of two unapproved peptides, in findings handed down on October 28 that now pressure Australia's medicines regulator to tighten the rules on a booming wellness market.

item.title: Samsung Is Shutting Down Samsung News in India and South Korea on December 21
item.description: Samsung has told Galaxy owners in India and South Korea that Samsung News will be discontinued on December 21, 2026, ending the built in news feed that has sat on the home screen of Galaxy phones and tablets since 2023, and users there who rely on it now have seven weeks to find a replacement.

item.title: Down 25, the Warriors Beat the Lakers 112-95 and Made NBA History
item.description: Stephen Curry scored 31 points and the Golden State Warriors erased a 25 point deficit to beat the Los Angeles Lakers 112-95 on October 30 in their NBA Cup opener at Chase Center. The comeback set a shot clock era record, and Curry passed Dominique Wilkins for 18th place on the NBA's all time scoring list along the way.

item.title: Binance Says $6.3 Billion Was Drained in a Security Incident, the Largest Crypto Theft on Record
item.description: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says about $6.3 billion in crypto was drained from its wallets on Thursday in what would be the largest theft in the industry's history. The exchange says about $3 billion has been frozen, that customer losses will be covered, and that withdrawals are suspended while it investigates.

item.title: Christian Watson Went to the Hospital Mid-Game. Then He Came Back and Finished It.
item.description: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson was taken by ambulance to a hospital during Thursday night's game against the Carolina Panthers. Then he came back, ran out of the locker room midway through the third quarter, and helped the Packers close out a 27-19 win at Lambeau Field.

item.title: Patrick Stewart, Captain Picard and Professor X, Dies at 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart, the Yorkshire-born Shakespearean actor who became Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, has died at 86. He died Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles, his family announced Thursday, after what it called a brief journey with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia.

item.title: Who Won the 2020 Election Trends Again Days Before the Midterms
item.description: Searches for who won the 2020 presidential election surged on Google Trends in the United States days before the November 3, 2026 midterm elections. The query rose into the 20,000-plus search band. The certified answer has been settled for years, which is what makes the spike itself the story.

item.title: Amazon posts $201.9 billion in third quarter sales as AWS growth jumps to 39%
item.description: Amazon reported third quarter net sales of $201.9 billion, up 12%, and operating income of $28.1 billion, its highest operating margin ever at 13.9%. AWS sales grew 39% to $46.0 billion, while net income slipped to $20.7 billion as last year's Anthropic gains did not repeat. The company guided fourth quarter sales of $240 billion to $247 billion.

item.title: Anthony Edwards to Miss Up to Two Months After Knee Procedure
item.description: Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee on October 29, 2026, and is expected to miss up to two months. The procedure cuts short the best start of his career, with Edwards averaging 33.3 points through four games for the 3-1 Timberwolves.

item.title: Apple Made a Touchscreen Mac. After More Than a Decade of Saying Never.
item.description: Apple introduced its first touchscreen Mac on October 28, 2026: a PROLED XDR MacBook Pro in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, starting at $2,899. It arrives one day after a cheaper M6 MacBook Pro, reversing a position Apple held for more than a decade.

item.title: Bears Land Jeffery Simmons in Blockbuster Trade With Titans
item.description: The Chicago Bears agreed to acquire All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans on Thursday, October 29, 2026, in a deal ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, sending two first-round picks to Tennessee. The trade was agreed Thursday morning and is pending a physical, and it pairs Simmons with a Chicago defense ranked among the league's best.

item.title: Brewers Won Their First World Series Behind Contreras
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 of the World Series on October 28, 2026, to win the first championship in franchise history. Catcher William Contreras was named World Series MVP after batting .381 in the five game series, with an RBI double in the clincher.

item.title: Dolores Huerta Died at 96 After Seven Decades of Organizing
item.description: Dolores Huerta, the labor leader who co-founded the United Farm Workers and coined Si, se puede, died on October 28, 2026, at her home in Bakersfield, California. She was 96. Her family said she died of cancer, and her death closed a seven decade career that reshaped farm labor in America.

item.title: DoorDash Buys Instacart in $17 Billion Grocery Delivery Deal
item.description: DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart on Thursday, October 29, 2026, in a deal worth about $17 billion, ending Instacart's run as an independent company and pairing the largest US food delivery app with the biggest grocery delivery platform. The companies announced a definitive agreement at $65 per share, with the deal expected to close in late 2027 or early 2028.

item.title: Ernie Johnson Announced His Final Season Hosting Inside the NBA
item.description: Ernie Johnson announced on October 28, 2026, that the 2026-27 season will be his last hosting Inside the NBA, ending a 37 season run at the desk. Johnson, 70, said the decision was his own, that he is not retiring outright, and that he will keep working on NCAA tournament coverage and other projects.

item.title: Giannis Wins First Game as a Heat Player as Bam Passes Haslem
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo won his first game as a Miami Heat player on October 28, 2026, scoring 24 points with 18 rebounds as Miami beat the Atlanta Hawks 129-117 in Atlanta. The win ended Miami's 0-4 start, and Bam Adebayo passed Udonis Haslem to become the Heat's all-time leading rebounder.

item.title: Alphabet Grew Revenue 25 Percent While AI Spending Outran Cash Flow
item.description: Alphabet reported revenue of $127.6 billion for the third quarter, up 25 percent, while operating income rose 30 percent to $40.6 billion. But the company spent $51.4 billion on property and equipment against $42.3 billion of operating cash flow, leaving free cash flow at negative $9.1 billion. Google stock drew more than 200,000 searches on Google Trends.

item.title: Netanyahu Rules Out an Arab-Backed Government. The Deadlock Continues.
item.description: Netanyahu has drawn his red line, and the count has confirmed the deadlock. With the regular count essentially complete, his bloc holds 53 seats, the opposition 48, and the Arab parties 19, leaving no camp near the 61 needed to govern. Netanyahu ruled out any government relying on Arab parties and demanded a strong right-wing government instead.

item.title: Jio Listed at a 21% Premium. India's Biggest IPO Ever.
item.description: Jio Platforms listed on October 28, 2026, opening at Rs 1,358 on the BSE and NSE, a 21.36% premium over its Rs 1,119 issue price, and closed at Rs 1,417.50 on the NSE and Rs 1,417.35 on the BSE, up about 26.7%. The Rs 30,213-crore IPO is India's largest ever, and the debut made Jio the country's second-most valuable listed company.

item.title: Jokic Records 200th Triple-Double as Nuggets Beat Pelicans
item.description: Nikola Jokic recorded his 200th career regular-season triple-double on October 28, 2026, finishing with 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists as the Denver Nuggets beat the New Orleans Pelicans 104-91 in New Orleans. Jokic became the second player in NBA history to reach 200, behind only Russell Westbrook.

item.title: Brunson Drops 38 as Knicks Erase 19-Point Deficit to Beat Bulls
item.description: Jalen Brunson scored 38 points as the defending champion New York Knicks erased a 19-point third-quarter deficit to beat the Chicago Bulls 133-127 on October 28, 2026, in Chicago. The win was New York's second in two nights after an 0-3 start, and it came with the bench carrying the comeback while starter Mikal Bridges sat.

item.title: Dallas Handed Oklahoma City Its First Loss of the Season, 120-96
item.description: The Dallas Mavericks beat the Oklahoma City Thunder 120-96 on October 28, 2026, at American Airlines Center, ending the Thunder's unbeaten start to the season. Cooper Flagg led Dallas with 26 points, eight assists and five rebounds without a turnover, while Oklahoma City fell to 4-1 and Dallas improved to 3-2.

item.title: FDA Classified the Miyoko's Plant Butter Recall as Class II
item.description: The Food and Drug Administration classified the recall of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter as Class II on October 23, 2026, after the product was pulled over yeast, mold and E. coli concerns. The recall covers 1,304 cases, or 7,824 individual units, sold in 10 states, and no illnesses have been reported.

item.title: North Korea Fired Cruise Missiles From Underwater. Its First Since 2024.
item.description: North Korea test-fired two submarine-launched strategic cruise missiles into the East Sea on October 14, 2026, its state news agency reported the next day. South Korea's military confirmed it tracked both launches. It was the North's first publicly reported underwater missile test since January 2024.

item.title: Rio's Deadliest Police Operation, One Year Later. The Toll Is 122.
item.description: Rio de Janeiro's state government first counted 64 people dead and 81 arrested in Operação Contenção, launched before dawn on October 28, 2025, against the Comando Vermelho gang in the Alemão and Penha favelas. That count later rose to 122 dead, and a year later the operation is back in the news.

item.title: Putin Hosted 22 African Leaders in Moscow. The Pitch Is a New World Order.
item.description: Vladimir Putin opened the third Russia-Africa summit in Moscow on October 28, 2026, with delegations from 48 African countries, 22 of them led by their leaders. His pitch was blunt: the Western-led order is ending, Russia is the partner that will help Africa profit from what replaces it, and the deals on grain, energy, and medicine prove it.

item.title: Two High-Speed Trains Collided in Spain. What We Know.
item.description: Two high-speed trains collided in central Spain on October 28, 2026, killing 68 people, according to the Castilla-La Mancha regional government. A Renfe AVE train struck the rear of a stationary Iryo train near Urda, derailing several carriages, two of which fell down an embankment. The government declared three days of official mourning while investigators establish what happened.

item.title: Drone Strike Hits Crowded Nyala Market as Death Toll Claims Diverge
item.description: A drone strike hit a busy market in Nyala, the capital of South Darfur, on the evening of October 26, 2026, and two counts of the dead now disagree by a wide margin. A Sudanese rights group says more than 100 people were killed. The hospital that Doctors Without Borders supports received 36 bodies. Neither figure has been independently verified.

item.title: Supreme Court Presses Election Commission Over Delhi's Missing Voters
item.description: India's Supreme Court pressed the Election Commission on October 28, 2026, over about 47 lakh Delhi voters missing from the draft electoral rolls. The court questioned why voters already on the rolls must file a first-timer's form to get back on them, and told the Commission not to let the October 30 deadline stand in the way.

item.title: Trump Says a Putin-Zelensky Meeting Is Coming 'Very Soon'.
item.description: President Donald Trump said a meeting between Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelensky will be set up 'very soon,' claiming a lot of progress toward ending the Russia-Ukraine war. He gave no date, location, or format, and neither Moscow nor Kyiv has confirmed that the two leaders agreed to meet.

item.title: The Final Week: Trump and Obama Are Rallying. The Polls Still Favor Democrats.
item.description: Six days before the November 3 midterms, the two final national polls point the same way: Democrats lead the race for Congress, voters say the economy is heading the wrong way, and both parties have sent their biggest names to the states that will decide control. Donald Trump is rallying in Ohio. Barack Obama is rallying in Georgia.

item.title: Lula Won. Bolsonaro Left. What Happens When Losing Means Leaving?
item.description: Lula won Brazil's presidential runoff, and his opponent left the country. The Superior Electoral Court confirmed 64,256,232 votes for Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, 51.79 percent of valid votes, against 59,826,041 for Flavio Bolsonaro, who refused to concede and has reportedly left Brazil for the United States instead.

item.title: The Fed Held Rates While Alphabet and Microsoft Paid Heavily for AI Growth
item.description: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75 to 4 percent on October 28, 2026, while Alphabet and Microsoft reported strong operating growth in the same quarter alongside heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure, and Amazon still to report.

item.title: Israel Voted. Nobody Won. Now the Coalition Talks Decide Everything.
item.description: Israelis voted on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, for the 26th Knesset, and nobody won. The count is still partial, the official results are not final, and no bloc holds the 61 seats a majority needs. What happens next will be decided in coalition talks, not at the ballot box.

item.title: Microsoft Offered 60,000 People Money to Leave. AI Is Paying for It.
item.description: On Monday, October 26, Microsoft offered about 60,000 employees money to leave. The Voluntary Exit Offer covers eligible staff at level 70 and below in the United States, Canada, India, and the United Kingdom. Microsoft did not announce a number; a company spokesperson confirmed about 60,000 people are eligible, roughly 27 percent of its workforce.

item.title: Trump Wants Venezuela as the 51st State. The Oil Came First.
item.description: The pitch. On Tuesday, October 27, 2026, President Donald Trump told a campaign rally in Corpus Christi, Texas, that Venezuela could become the 51st state of the United States, pointing to a tanker carrying 1 million barrels of Venezuelan crude that he called the greatest oil-related victory in history.

item.title: The $137 million question: if voters cannot tell what is real, what is left to trust?
item.description: AI generated ads have crossed $137 million in the 2026 US midterms, according to reporting on Oct 27, 2026. Most spending came from Republican candidates and allied groups, and only 27 percent of these ads say they are made by AI. Through Oct 11, 220 deepfake cases were found in 34 states. The total is not the story; it tells you AI ads are no longer an experiment, and the problem is national, not one state or one race. This post is not about whether AI ads should be banned. It asks a simpler question: if voters cannot tell what is real, what happens to trust in the next election after this one?

item.title: When an AI Lab Goes Public, Who Does It Answer To?
item.description: Anthropic filed to go public on October 26, 2026. The company behind Claude is now on the path to a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT, with the share count and the price range not yet set and the registration not yet effective. A filing is not a listing. It is a public statement of intent.

item.title: The Fed Meets, Big Tech Reports, and AI Has to Show Its Receipts

item.title: Trump Is Waiting Until After the Midterms. What Changes on Nov. 4?
item.description: Trump has made it clear there will be no attacks on Iran before the midterm elections. The attacks are not ruled out, only ruled out for now, and that difference is the whole story. The election is next Tuesday, Nov. 3, and the day after, Nov. 4, is when the constraint holding this back disappears.
